subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should this be solved as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated marker, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance and heartbeat authority design?
rationale: The choice changes host-elevated exec authority for persisted cron jobs, heartbeat runs, config/state migration, and existing wildcard internal-source setups, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat this as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design and keep heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now with explicit create, update, execution, migration, and audit coverage.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove cron-event and heartbeat wildcard elevation unless maintainers intentionally preserve a compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design and keep heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent caller-scope work is the closest current scheduling provenance path and already established the adjacent Gateway/agent cron boundary.
